A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlexRank and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. The material supports a reliable comparison across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and MNIST experiments, language-model and vision evaluations, downstream adaptation results, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, rank-selection diagnostics, and GPU runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The DataSVD initialization, nested DP rank selection, and distillation procedure are retained. GAR names and elaborates the identity-block inference reparametrization already described in v1 Section 3.5. Algorithms 1–3 add procedural documentation rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: The synthetic/MNIST, FineWebEdu, commonsense, ImageNet1K, and math/code training and evaluation coverage is retained. The added experiments examine rank-selection reliability and execution efficiency of existing operations rather than introducing new datasets or application tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds LLM-PRUNER, LAYERSKIP, and independently trained FlexRank configurations to the Llama-3.2-1B comparison. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparators beyond the retained SVD/DataSVD/ACIP comparisons. v1's independent-model controls concerned different experiments.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ten independently trained models receiving 10% each of the total training budget, exact-budget rank-selection diagnostics, and GPU forward-pass timing across active ranks. The existing NLP/CV training recipes and downstream zero-/few-shot settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3/Figure 9 tests additive-probe ranking agreement, exact-budget selection success, and regret on failures. Figure 5 adds a matched-budget weight-sharing control, while Appendix D.4/Figure 10 tests practical GAR efficiency. The earlier GPT-2 ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same uncertainty values. v2 adds no reported seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its new correlations, violation rates, and regret distributions are diagnostic evaluation results rather than changes to uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds comparison and runtime results in Figures 5 and 10. Figure 9 reports Spearman correlation 0.991, pairwise violations 3.70%, exact-budget matches 94.1%, and maximum relative regret 11.58%. Table 1's existing math/code results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The main theorems and Appendix B proofs are retained. Section 3.5 corrects the gauge identity from (UG)(VG^-1)^T to (UG)(G^-1V^T), and Section 2.1 removes the expectation from the budget constraint. Appendix C.1 also introduces an apparent self-referential residual-definition typo.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly elevates GAR to a contribution and reframes the theoretical contribution around nested training and near-optimal rank selection. The central train-once deployment and accuracy–cost claims in the abstract and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of knowledge transfer across budgets, clarifies the ranking-preservation interpretation already mentioned in v1 Appendix C.2, and discusses factorization memory/training overhead and compute-bound inference conditions. Existing limitations concerning data, optimization, and unevaluated adaptive routing remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, detailed pipeline and DP pseudocode, explicit GAR use across rank-based baselines, and RTX5090/torch.compile timing details. Conversely, v1 Appendix D.4's specific A100 node counts and training-duration estimates disappear. Core hyperparameter recipes remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds LLM-PRUNER and concurrent work by Rauba and van der Schaar, explaining distinctions in decomposition, selection, and GAR. It removes the SPDY reference and revises its novelty positioning toward theoretical foundations. The updated Genzel reference describes the same ACIP work.

P1.justification: The introduction is condensed, contributions and method-stage descriptions are rewritten, Section 7 gains topical subsections, and an appendix contents page is added. Most section ordering, exposition, and proof text remain; the editing does not amount to a wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 4–5 are merged into v2 Figure 4. New Figures 5, 9, and 10 and three algorithm displays substantially expand the presentation; other plots are redrawn, heatmaps relabeled, and tables relocated. Figure 4 incorrectly labels its retained relative parameter scale as absolute.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central rank-selection and deployment claims through direct ranking diagnostics, measured GPU efficiency, broader baselines, and matched-budget controls. Detailed pseudocode and code-access information also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removal of training-resource estimates and the introduced labeling/notation errors, although the new validation remains limited to its reported settings.
